reading_title_html: It Is Essential That the Master Be Present

reading.rtitle: It Is Essential That the Master Be Present
paras: Port state control exists because a flag state cannot inspect a ship that is never in its waters. The regime requires that every vessel calling at a member port be liable to inspection, and that any deficiency found be recorded against the ship rather than against the inspector who found it. Detention follows only where the deficiency is such that the vessel is not, in the view of the officer, seaworthy.

The convention requires that the master notify the maritime authority immediately of any condition affecting seaworthiness, and recommends that all crew members complete the relevant drill before departure. Note the form of both verbs: notify and complete, not notifies and completes. Formal regulatory English uses the base form after requires, recommends, demands and it is essential that, and a reader who does not recognise it will find a plural where there is a singular, or a past where there is none.

A certificate is issued by, or on behalf of, the flag state, and an endorsement records an additional competency the seafarer has demonstrated. A surveyor acting under authorisation may issue both. What the surveyor may not do is decide that a deficiency is unimportant: that judgement belongs to the authority, and the distinction is the reason detentions are reviewed by somebody who never saw the ship.

The system is criticised for the obvious reason. A vessel may hold every certificate the law requires and still be unseaworthy on the morning of the inspection, and no document detects that. What port state control does is narrower and more useful than the criticism allows: it makes the cost of a deficiency fall on the ship that has it, in the port where it is found, on the day it is found. It is essential that it stay that way.

reading2_title_html: Text Two: Not a Ship in Sight

paras: For most of the history of measurement a standard was an object. The metre was a bar of platinum-iridium kept near Paris, and the kilogram was a cylinder of the same alloy kept beside it. Anyone who wished to know what a kilogram was could, in principle, go and look at one.

The difficulty with an object is that it changes. The prototype kilogram lost mass over a century, or the copies distributed to national laboratories gained it; from inside the system there was no way to tell which, because the prototype was the definition and a definition cannot drift. It is essential, in a measurement system, that the standard be independent of the thing it measures.

The solution adopted in 2019 was to define the remaining physical units in terms of constants of nature. The kilogram is now fixed by the Planck constant, the metre by the speed of light and the second by a transition in caesium. Nothing is kept in a vault. Any laboratory with the right equipment can realise the unit from first principles, and two laboratories that disagree now know that one of them is wrong.

It is worth noticing what was not achieved. The new definitions are not more accurate for ordinary purposes, and a kitchen scale is exactly as good as it was. What changed is that the system no longer depends on the survival of one particular piece of metal, which is a different kind of improvement altogether: the sort that becomes visible only when something is lost.

grammar_question: Three of these have a singular subject and a verb with no s, and one uses be where you would expect is. Say what the four have in common in the words that come BEFORE the that.
grammar_rows: the verb in the that-clause goes into the BASE form, whatever the subject
The Code requires that the master notify the authority.
it is essential / vital / imperative that
same base form, in the impersonal construction regulations prefer
It is essential that the standard be independent.
the base form of be is be, in every person
requires that every vessel be liable to inspection
not goes straight in front of the base form, with no auxiliary
requires that the master not sail without clearance

the base form looks like a plural, a typing error, or a missing auxiliary, and every one of those misreadings is offered to you as an option. Requires that the master notifies is not the same sentence: it is not regulatory English at all, and choosing it means you did not recognise the form.
grammar_insight: The subjunctive survives in English almost only where somebody is being told what to do. That is why a regulation is full of it and a newspaper is not -- and why recognising it is worth more marks than it looks.

listenings.sub: A port state control officer on the only judgement that is his. Sound first -- no text.
listenings.text: I am asked constantly whether I enjoy detaining ships. I have detained eleven vessels in nine years, and I did not enjoy any of them. What people misunderstand is how narrow my decision actually is. I record what I find. If a lifeboat release gear has not been serviced, that is a deficiency and it goes on the record whether the master agrees with me or not. What I do not decide is whether it matters. The regime requires that any deficiency found be recorded against the ship, and it requires that detention follow only where the vessel is not seaworthy. Those are two different sentences and I am only responsible for the first one. The second is reviewed by a person in an office who has never seen that ship, and that is not a weakness of the system. It is the whole design.
questions: How many vessels has he detained, and over how long?
Eleven vessels in nine years, and he says he did not enjoy any of them.
What does he record, and what does he not decide?
He records what he finds -- an unserviced lifeboat release gear is a deficiency whether the master agrees or not. He does not decide whether it matters.
Why does he say the review by somebody who never saw the ship is not a weakness?
Because it is the whole design: recording the deficiency and deciding whether it justifies detention are two different responsibilities.

listenings.sub: The examiner returns, on the three mistakes of the harder texts. Sound first -- no text.
listenings.text: In the first block I told you that marks go on degree, agency and register. In the second block a fourth appears, and it is the one that separates the good candidates from the very good ones. It is structure. A relative clause attached to the wrong noun, a cleft that you read as an ordinary sentence, a subjunctive that you take for a typing error. None of those is a vocabulary problem, and none of them can be fixed by reading faster. They are fixed by slowing down at exactly four places: after a comma that introduces a which, after the word that, before any verb that has no ending, and at the first word of a sentence that begins with a negative adverb. Four places in a whole paper. That is the entire technique, and candidates who use it stop losing the marks they were losing.
questions: What were the three mistakes of the first block, and what is the fourth?
Degree, agency and register. The fourth, which separates good candidates from very good ones, is structure.
What three structural mistakes does she name?
A relative clause attached to the wrong noun, a cleft read as an ordinary sentence, and a subjunctive taken for a typing error.
Where does she say a candidate should slow down?
After a comma that introduces a which, after the word that, before any verb with no ending, and at the first word of a sentence beginning with a negative adverb.

pc_desc: Everything from Block 2 under exam conditions, plus the subjunctive of regulatory English. Key words: maritime authority, surveyor, certificate, endorsement, port state control, deficiency, detention, seafarer, competency, seaworthiness. Structure: the subjunctive in formal regulatory language.

paras: The regime requires that every vessel calling at a member port be liable to inspection, and that any deficiency found be recorded against the ship. The convention requires that the master notify the maritime authority immediately of any condition affecting seaworthiness.

It recommends that all crew members complete the relevant drill before departure, and that the master not sail without clearance. It is essential that the standard be independent of the thing it measures, and it is essential that the cost of a deficiency stay with the ship that has it.

quiz.q: The convention requires that the master notify the authority. Why is there no s on notify?
opts: It is a printing error that has survived in the text.
It is the subjunctive: the base form after require, whatever the subject.
Because master is treated as a plural in legal English.

quiz.q: How would you write the negative of requires that the master sail with clearance?
opts: requires that the master does not sail without clearance
requires that the master not sail without clearance
requires that the master no sail without clearance

quiz.q: It is essential that the standard be independent. Why be and not is?
opts: Because be is the base form, and the base form is what this construction takes.
Because standard is an uncountable noun.
Because the sentence describes the future.

grammar_tip_lead: English kept the subjunctive almost only where somebody is being told what to do. That is why a regulation is full of it and a newspaper is not -- and why a verb with no ending, in a formal text, is a signal rather than a mistake.

teacher.s1: Abertura (1 min): Aula de SIMULADO que fecha o bloco 2. DECISAO DE DESENHO do programa: toda aula e reading-driven (a REGRA 29.2 nao se aplica aqui), porque a prova e 100% leitura. Formato da prova real: DOIS textos, um deles sem navio nenhum. Entre direto, sem cumprimento scriptado (REGRA 27A).
teacher.s2: Warm-up (3 min): Ela classificou dez frases em finding, hedge e testimony. Peca duas e a PALAVRA que decidiu. Se ela apontar a palavra sem hesitar, a aula 9 pegou.
teacher.s3: Provocacao (4 min): A clausula e real e o verbo nao tem s. Espere. Se ela disser 'erro de digitacao', voce encontrou exatamente o que a prova explora. A segunda pergunta (o que mudaria com 'notifies') e a mais importante: nada mudaria no sentido, mas deixaria de ser ingles regulatorio -- e a opcao errada e sempre essa.
teacher.s4: Objetivo (1 min): Diga: the words of an inspection, one verb form, and a debrief about reasons.
teacher.s5: Transicao vocab (1 min): Diga: Ten words that decide whether a ship sails tomorrow. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s6: Vocab reveal 1-4 (5 min): maritime authority, surveyor, certificate, endorsement. NAO traduza (REGRA 13). CCQ para endorsement: Is an endorsement a separate document? (Nao -- e uma ADICAO ao certificado.) CCQ para surveyor: Who does the surveyor work for? (Atua sob autorizacao do flag state -- e nao decide se a falha importa.)
teacher.s7: Vocab reveal 5-7 (5 min): port state control, deficiency, detention. CCQ para port state control: Why does it exist at all? (Porque o flag state nao consegue inspecionar navio que nunca entra nas aguas dele -- e a primeira frase do texto.) CCQ para deficiency: Is a deficiency the same as a detention? (Nao -- uma pode existir sem a outra.)
teacher.s8: Vocab reveal 8-10 (5 min): seafarer, competency, seaworthiness. CCQ para seafarer: Does seafarer include the cook? (Sim -- qualquer pessoa empregada a bordo, em qualquer funcao.) CCQ para competency: Is a competency a course? (Nao -- e a capacidade DEMONSTRADA, e essa distincao ja caiu.)
teacher.s9: Consolidate (4 min): Ela toca a palavra e le a definicao em voz alta antes de fechar o par.
teacher.s10: Transicao (1 min): Diga: The clock starts now. Fifteen minutes for this text and its questions. O proximo slide e o de TAREFA: as perguntas ANTES do texto.
teacher.s11: Texto 1 -- SOB RELOGIO (8 min): Cronometre de verdade, diga o tempo a cada 5 minutos, e fique CALADO. Nao ajude, nao traduza, nao responda pergunta. Anote onde ela para.
teacher.s12: Gist (2 min): Ela escolhe e justifica. A opcao (a) e a critica que o texto RESPONDE, nao a tese dele.
teacher.s13: True or False (5 min): Ainda sob relogio. Responde as cinco e SO DEPOIS confere. A 2 e a 5 sao trocas de AGENTE (inspector x ship; quem revisa).
teacher.s14: Transicao gramatica (1 min): Diga: The verb from slide 3 is in that text eleven times. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s15: Grammar discovery (6 min): Nao de a regra. Pergunte o que vem ANTES do 'that' nos quatro exemplos (requires, requires, recommends, it is essential that). So entao clique Reveal the Rule. CCQ decisivo: is 'requires that the master notifies' the same sentence? (Nao -- deixa de ser ingles regulatorio.) Ela estuda gramatica sozinha: aqui e reconhecimento, nao producao.
teacher.s16: Practice (3 min): Ela diz a forma ORALMENTE antes de clicar. O quinto item e o NEGATIVO (not sail, sem does).
teacher.s17: Spot the error (3 min): Os quatro sao a forma indicativa no lugar da subjuntiva. Repare que todas as frases 'erradas' soam naturais -- e por isso que este e o item mais dificil da prova.
teacher.s18: Transicao equivalencia (1 min): Diga: Same two texts, other words. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s19: Como a prova esconde (3 min): O quarto par ('a kitchen scale is exactly as good as it was' -> 'everyday measurement was unaffected') e do texto NAO-maritimo, e e o tipo de parafrase que a prova de 2025 usou.
teacher.s20: Equivalencia (4 min): Depois de fechar os pares, cubra a direita e faca a direcao dificil.
teacher.s21: Complete (4 min): Teacher-led, uma lacuna por vez. As oito respostas sao oito das dez palavras da aula.
teacher.s22: Quick fire (5 min): Uma por vez, em voz alta, antes das dicas. A quarta e do texto 2 e testa se ela leu o segundo texto com o mesmo cuidado que o primeiro.
teacher.s22a: Texto 2 -- SOB RELOGIO (7 min): Sem navio nenhum, de proposito -- a prova de 2025 abriu com um texto da Britannica sobre IA. Cronometre. NAO ajude. Se ela reclamar do assunto, anote e use no debrief: a reclamacao E o achado.
teacher.s22b: True or False do texto 2 (5 min): Mesma regra da casa. A afirmacao 4 e de GRAU (nao ficou mais preciso para uso comum) e a 2 e de ESCOPO (de dentro do sistema nao dava para saber).
teacher.s23: Transicao debrief (1 min): Diga: Now the part that is worth more than the score. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s24: Listening 1 (5 min): LEIA AS 3 PERGUNTAS EM VOZ ALTA COM ELA ANTES de tocar (REGRA 2.1). Escuta medida em 0%: 0.75x na primeira vez. O oficial usa a subjuntiva duas vezes -- peca que ela ache as duas na segunda escuta.
teacher.s25: Listening 2 (5 min): LEIA AS 3 PERGUNTAS EM VOZ ALTA COM ELA ANTES de tocar (REGRA 2.1). Este audio entrega a TECNICA das quatro paradas. Peca que ela repita as quatro sem olhar -- e o que ela leva para os simulados seguintes.
teacher.s26: Debrief guiado (5 min): Tres questoes, com linha de evidencia e o defeito de cada distrator. Exija a linha; 'achei que era' nao conta.
teacher.s27: Debrief semi-livre (5 min): As quatro paradas, praticadas num paragrafo que ela ja entendeu. E treino de PROCEDIMENTO, nao de compreensao -- corrija o procedimento, nao a resposta.
teacher.s28: Producao livre (5 min): Nao interrompa. Mede-se: tres mecanicas NOMEADAS com exemplo. Se ela ainda descrever em sentimento ('fico insegura'), esse e o achado do bloco e vira o foco do bloco 3.
teacher.s29: Transicao wrap-up (1 min): Diga: Block two, closed.
teacher.s30: Survival card (3 min): As cinco frases sao subjuntivas. Toque e peca repeticao: dizer 'that the master notify' em voz alta e o que faz o ouvido parar de corrigir para 'notifies'.
teacher.s31: Checklist (2 min): Leia cada item em voz alta. Os 5 checks fecham a aula e acendem o stamp.
teacher.s32: Encerramento (2 min): Diga: Block two complete, Helena. HOMEWORK ORALMENTE, nunca escrito na tela: (1) achar cinco subjuntivas em texto regulatorio real em ingles (SOLAS, STCW, ISM) e reescrever cada uma na forma indicativa, dizendo o que se perde; (2) refazer as questoes de hoje que ela errou, escrevendo ao lado de cada distrator qual das quatro mecanicas ele usou.
